findings.description: `open_game` returns `null` without calling `push_error` when `host.session_config()` is empty, while `record_coast` silently returns `false` for invalid shader tier, visual quality, quads or meshes, water layer, day, or zoom. These setup failures reach `_run` as either a bare exit code 1 or the generic “four complete coast passes” error, leaving operators unable to identify the cause from the log or capture folder—particularly on a phone without a console.

evidence.explanation: The empty-session-config check in `open_game` returns null without a message, and its caller in `coast_pan.gd` quits with status 1 when the game is null. In `record_coast`, the listed precondition checks return false silently; only the coverage check at line 100 has its own message, so the other failures reach the caller’s generic check failure. The README instructs desktop users to set the shader-tier environment variable, making an omitted `PK_MOBILE_SHADER_TIER` an expected path into a silent return.

findings.description: `load_capture` in `report.py` special-cases the outcome string `29 checks, 2 failures` and then overwrites the platform, model, build, screen size and Godot version of the four captured arms with values from `iphone-16e.json`, so a run that failed its own checks is reported as a valid iPhone result. The same change lowers the VSync expectation from disabled to enabled in `coast_pan.gd`, so the failing assertion is changed to match the observed result instead of the cause being explained. Any later reader of the reference will trust the metadata that was injected rather than measured, and the exception is only protected by a hash match on four files.
findings.title: Failed benchmark run accepted as a valid baseline

findings.description: The exploration setup in `_prepare_explored_map` advances background days by polling `host._runtime_commit_day` with `process_frame` and then asserts on it, without `wait_for_runtime_day` and without the host's `_service_runtime_liveness` receive step. Completion is therefore defined by the observed committed field rather than by the production result-receive path, which can make the assertions depend on frame timing.

findings.description: `matched_timings()` collects surface IDs from every present request in the trace, then accepts display swaps containing any of those IDs without pairing a swap to its corresponding request. When a traced surface appears in another swap during the measured window, the count check can reject a valid trace or accept 110 swaps that do not represent the measured frames.
findings.title: Screen timing can include unrelated swaps

evidence.explanation: Requests retain timestamps, command-buffer keys, and surface IDs, whereas the swap filter uses the union of surface IDs from all requests and discards swap identity. The later validation establishes only that 110 timestamps were selected, not that they correspond to the 110 measured requests.

A run from another engine version, or another phone given the same `--device` label, can therefore receive `comparable: true` and direct timing deltas against the iPhone reference.

findings.description: `GameSettings._ready()` skips `load_settings()` for a coast-pan run, leaving defaults in memory, while a later persisting `update()` saves that entire dictionary. If a tester changes a setting through the game UI or a game command during the desktop run, the next normal launch reads defaults in place of previously saved preferences.
findings.title: Benchmark runs can overwrite saved settings
